articles.title: New Steph Curry Rumors Reveal Warriors' Presentation to Convince Star to Sign Historic Contract
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors and Stephen Curry have plenty of familiarity with one another, but the organization made sure to be thorough when it pitched the 12-time All-Star on a new contract.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors and Stephen Curry have plenty of familiarity with one another, but the organization made sure to be thorough when it pitched the 12-time All-Star on a new contract.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Friday that Curry agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension. According to colleague Anthony Slater , Golden State tabled "several contract choices in recent weeks, including the option to wait."

"As part of the Warriors' presentation to Curry, the team laid out various paths that included the idea of a slight pay cut from his max, delivering them more salary cap room to build a contender around him in the future, team sources said," per Slater.

Curry is on the books for $62.6 million in 2026-27, while his new deal averages $58 million annually. A little cap savings can go a long way, especially for a team that's a consistently high spender.

Jimmy Butler, Draymond Green and Brandin Podziemski combine to have a cap hold of $124 million in 2027-28. Depending on how the Warriors handle those three, they could have some serious cash to spend next summer.

Some heavy hitters could be hitting the market at that time. Nikola Jokić, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Karl-Anthony Towns, Kevin Durant and Rudy Gobert all have player options. Michael Porter Jr., Tyler Herro and RJ Barrett will be unrestricted free agents outright.

Since winning the 2022 NBA Finals, Golden State has missed the playoffs twice and failed to advance past the second round in the two years it reached the postseason.

Curry continues to play at a high level relative to his age (38), but he's clearly not at his peak anymore. For other stars around the NBA, the allure of teaming up with the two-time MVP isn't the same as it was five years ago.

Perhaps the organization's championship window is shut for good. Even if that's the case, the front office is determined to go down fighting and surround Curry with as strong a supporting cast as possible.

articles.title: New Warriors Rumors on Draymond Green, Jimmy Butler's Contracts After Stephen Curry's Historic Deal
articles.summary: One Golden State Warriors star removed the questions over his short-term future, and that casts a bigger spotlight on the franchise's other two marquee names.
articles.body:
One Golden State Warriors star removed the questions over his short-term future, and that casts a bigger spotlight on the franchise's other two marquee names.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Stephen Curry agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension. He can opt out after the 2027-28 NBA season.

This gives general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. a better idea of the payroll with Jimmy Butler and Draymond Green on expiring deals. The Athletic's Nick Friedell reported the pair "have expressed interest in retiring with the Warriors, though doing so could require them to return on substantially smaller contracts."

Curry left some money on the table, roughly $20 million on a two-year max.

That didn't amount to a massive pay cut, though. The 12-time All-Star will make $62.6 million for the upcoming season and then average $58 million over the next two years.

Butler and Green — the former in particular — might have to sacrifice more in order to extend their time in the Bay Area.

Butler is signed for $56.8 million and has a $65.5 million cap hold for 2027-28. It's difficult to envision a scenario where the Warriors are paying him more than Curry, and his market will inevitably reflect the fact he's a 37-year-old coming off a torn ACL.

Green is likewise on the wrong end of the aging curve and has seen his skills gradually decline. He remains an effective two-way player but doesn't register the impact he did during the peak of the Warriors' dynasty.

In the case of Green, the extent of his pay cut will at least be a little less due to the fact he'll collect half ($27.7 million) of what Butler will.

Through the departure of Klay Thompson in 2024, Dunleavy outlined his and the Warriors' priorities. They're desperate to win another championship with Curry, and that might mean parting ways with key stars who helped deliver a lot of success.

When the time comes to seriously negotiate extensions with Butler and Green, the front office will have a clear limit to how much it's willing to spend. If the two veterans want to maximize what earning power they still have, that could mean putting on a different uniform in 2027.

articles.title: 2026 WNBA Playoff Preview: The case for all eight teams to win it all
articles.summary: In an incredibly close WNBA playoff field, who has the edge?
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA regular season has officially been written and the playoffs are now the time for one team to seal its legacy with a championship when it’s all said and done by late October.

For the first time in a long time, it’s not super clear who the front runner is to raise the WNBA Finals trophy, due to major trends that we have been tracking all season including offenses being more efficient , and more league wide parity as a result of expansion.

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve, who will be a part of the WNBA postseason for now 26 out of 30 total playoffs, dove into the type of anomaly that exists in this year’s playoff field. She doesn’t really see a clear favorite to win it all like in previous seasons.

“We have a 26-win team that’s the eight seed,” Reeve said on Thursday night after the Lynx ended their regular season. “The field I think is it really doesn’t matter what seed you are, having home court advantage obviously we all fight for that. There’s a reason you fight for that. But no, I don’t think anybody should be surprised by any outcomes … I wouldn’t be surprised by anything that happens because I think all the teams are that good.”

Cheryl Reeve on the competition level in this years playoffs “You have a 26 win team, that’s the 8 seed... the field it really doesn’t matter what seed you are, having home court advantage obviously we all fight for that… I don’t think anybody should be surprised by any… pic.twitter.com/UQcViRKi8G — Andrew Dukowitz (@adukeMN) September 25, 2026

Cheryl Reeve on the competition level in this years playoffs “You have a 26 win team, that’s the 8 seed... the field it really doesn’t matter what seed you are, having home court advantage obviously we all fight for that… I don’t think anybody should be surprised by any… pic.twitter.com/UQcViRKi8G

Reeve is spot-on when she says that the field is wide open and this was especially backed up by the fact that it took until the very last day of the regular season for seeding to be solidified, which made a lot of the final games of the regular season littered with consequence. These eight teams were jockeying for positioning all week long .

To be clear, this isn’t a matchup based playoff preview, but I will consider where teams are placed according to their seeding on the playoff bracket to make some determinations. For each team I ask and answer three questions, based on what needs to happen for each team to win the title or get bounced early in addition to who each team’s X-Factor throughout the postseason will be.

Let’s begin in order of when each team will begin their playoff journey on Sunday, starting with the teams that play at 2 p.m. ET all the way down to those that play their first playoff game at 9 p.m. ET.

The team can play connected enough defense consistently throughout games. The Liberty’s defense ranked seventh this season, the lowest since 2022. While they’ve had impressive individual moments especially when Breanna Stewart and Leonie Fiebich and Jonquel Jones are focused and communicating at a high level, that hasn’t happened nearly enough this season.

The Liberty will have an early round playoff exit if…

New York is exactly who they’ve been during the regular season. I could probably write a whole other story about the Liberty’s confusing season. While New York has had some uncontrollable injuries, especially in Satou Sabally, and then seven weeks without Leonie Fiebich, there have been moments when the team has looked confused and lacking cohesion, leaving Breanna Stewart having to do a lot of heavy lifting. A first round exit for a second season in a row will be deemed a huge disappointment for the franchise.

This is an unconventional choice, but Sabrina Ionescu has had a down year, averaging the least amount of points scored since her first full season in the WNBA back in 2021. Ionescu’s season was hampered by two injuries: an ankle issue and then a back injury that she dealt with back-to-back before she made her season debut. She has been consistently inconsistent with some clutch shooting games, including in the Commissioner’s Cup championship back in late June, and a two week stretch in late July into early August when she shot over 60 percent from the field over five games. If Ionescu can regain some semblance of her previous self, she gives the Liberty a much higher chance of moving onto the second round.

Both Olivia Miles and Napheesa Collier are healthy enough and can find the right offensive balance between the two stars. Miles was sidelined for the final two games of the regular season due to a strain in her left calf. Collier is still gaining her footing especially defensively after being out for more than half of the regular season. There have been moments down the stretch of the regular season when she’s turned the ball over and hasn’t quite played in rhythm. Some of this could be due to the fact that both she and Miles still haven’t played all that many minutes together. This lack of synergy became apparent in the Lynx’s most recent regular game against the Liberty when Miles took so many more shots than Collier, and Collier had an advantage being defended often on switches by wing Leonie Fiebich.

The Lynx will have an early round playoff exit if…

The defense doesn’t return closer to its form from the first two months of the season. Throughout the first 18 games of the season the Lynx boasted a defense that was rated below 98. But the next 21 games told a completely different story and their defensive rating ballooned to over 108 over July and August before returning to under 104 amongst the team’s four games in September.

Nia Brodie (née Coffey) has made a considerable impact in the Lynx’s 33 wins this season. She shot the three ball at a 43.1 percent clip in wins versus 22.9 percent in losses. Her plus/minus was also +5.5 during Lynx wins and -3.9 in losses. Brodie’s shooting and defensive versatility are going to be integral especially when the Lynx are going to face much more size on their side of the bracket.

The team buys into defending the basketball at a higher level. The Fever finished the regular season with the eighth best defensive rating. Fever head coach Stephanie White noted back in August that she believes her team needs to be better defensively for them to be a true contender. Kelsey Mitchell’s defense has improved drastically and Caitlin Clark’s has improved in spurts. But will that be enough?

The Fever will have an early round playoff exit if…

Aliyah Boston isn’t healthy enough to play like herself. Boston is the team’s defensive anchor and she is one of few who can defend A’ja Wilson exceptionally. But if Boston’s nagging leg injury persists—she left the Fever’s last game of the regular season early due to it—how effective can she be not just in the first round but also beyond?

I’ve written before about how the emergence of Makayla Timpson has stabilized the Fever’s front court. Her combo of athleticism and cutting ability could give opponents fits especially when defenses are going to be locked in on the Fever’s big three in Clark, Mitchell and Boston. Against the Las Vegas Aces especially, the Timpson is going to have ample opportunity to really show out especially when the Aces will most likely play smaller lineups since NaLyssa Smith ended her season with a knee injury.

They can repeat their approach to the defensive end of the ball from last postseason. Back in 2025, the Aces finished with the eighth best defensive rating. But then when it mattered most, the Aces executed head coach Becky Hammon’s more creative defensive schemes and defended harder than they did during the regular season.

The Aces will have an early round playoff exit if…

Their role players don’t over achieve. What was impressive in 2025 was even when stars Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray didn’t play at their absolute best, Las Vegas had key offensive performances from Dana Evans, Smith and Jewell Loyd to take some of the pressure off. A year later Evans only played in 14 regular season games meanwhile Smith is out for the season. It’s not for sure if Cheyenne Parker-Tyus, Brianna Turner, Stephanie Talbot and Mai Yamamoto can be relied upon consistently on the offensive end.

Loyd has had her least productive season in her 12 year WNBA career, but that could render meaningless if she steps up in the postseason. Against the Mercury in the Aces final regular season game, Loyd scored 25 points off the bench on 9-of-14 shooting. That level of efficiency is going to be integral for the Aces to defend their title.

Are the Young Hos — or who I coined Gen Z’s team — the WNBA’s team of destiny? Shakira Austin has looked at times like a potential MVP candidate at moments throughout this season. Sonia Citron has also played in so many clutch situations during the regular season and has racked up 115 minutes and 85 points in clutch time. Those are both the most across the entire league. If those two play at their level or even above in addition to fearless play from Kiki Iriafen, the Mystics could continue to be a problem as they were during the regular season. Also, if their head coach Sydney Johnson proves he can make decisions down the stretch that are shrewd and put pressure on his opponent, watch out.

The Mystics will have an early round playoff exit if…

Institutional precedent remains the same. While the Mystics are the youngest team in WNBA history to make the playoffs, that doesn’t guarantee a deep run. League history might not look on them so fondly. It’s hard to remember in recent memory a team that was so young that made it all the way to the WNBA finals. Veteran leadership and experience is absolutely critical when it comes to winning titles. And while the Mystics have a WNBA champion in Betnijah Laney-Hamilton on roster, Johnson has never coached in a professional postseason series before.

Rookie point guard Georgia Amoore’s development has been one of many Mystics success stories. From May through June, Amoore wasn’t shooting more than 30 percent from three. But then in August a switch flipped and she shot over 40 percent from deep in 12 games. That momentum continued into the four regular season games in September as Amoore shot 57.1 percent from three and averaged 11.3 points. If Amoore is knocking down shots regularly in the playoffs, the math of the Mystics’ offense changes drastically.

Last year’s core group which includes Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray, Jordin Canada, Naz Hillmon and now second year head coach Karl Smesko all learn from their mistakes in year one. Will Gray play through her frustrations instead of letting them affect her play? Can Howard score in clutch time? Will Smesko have the situational awareness to make adjustments proactively so that what happened a year ago doesn’t happen again?

The Dream will have an early round playoff exit if…

Angel Reese struggles in the postseason. Reese will be participating in her first playoffs and there are bound to be some growing pains. If the Dream’s defensive anchor and player with the highest motor struggles to play well through the challenges that come with a high pressure playoff environment, the Dream are going to struggle. Especially when what Atlanta is so good defensively is built around her strengths.

DeWanna Bonner, who the Dream added just around a month ago, is someone who possesses skills Atlanta desperately needed. She balances their offense with her outside shooting from the forward spot but she provides a veteran voice and set of experiences that most of the roster doesn’t have. The Dream are one of the most talented groups on paper, but they still lack WNBA playoffs experience. The team lacked composure down the stretch in last season’s first round, which allowed the injured but deeply bought-in Indiana Fever to advance.

They defend like they did playing at home. It is striking how much worse the Dallas Wings defended when they were on the road compared to when they were at home. During the 2026 regular season, Dallas’ road game defensive resting was 112.9. Meanwhile for their 22 games at home, however, that rate went all the way below 100 to 99.9.

The Wings will have an early round playoff exit if…

They don’t have a fourth scorer in double figures. Paige Bueckers, Arike Ogwunbowale and Jessica Shepard are going to score the basketball. But the question remains — who else does and can do so consistently, especially when opposing defenses are going to be glued to Bueckers? Without Azzi Fudd available, the Wings have a major scoring hole, and it’s not clear who will step up to the challenge consistently in a playoff series.

Although the Wings’ playoff X-Factor is…

Awak Kuier, the Wings’ forward who also has a good case for most improved player alongside her teammate and front runner Shepard, has played multiple roles for Dallas during the regular season. She began coming off the bench and then was a starter once it was clear that Alanna Smith was seriously struggling on her new team. Kuier has been functioning as a rim protector, perimeter defender on switches and a floor spacer. She shot 39 percent from three on over 82 attempts during the regular season. As I’ve written previously , she’s filling an ironic roster gap since Fudd ended her season with surgery.

Their consistency on the defensive end doesn’t falter and they successfully make it messy. Back when current Wings general manager Curt Miller coached the Connecticut Sun, he used to use the phrase “make it messy” to describe how his blue collar teams had to play to find success and disrupt more free flowing offenses in the postseason. This mentality took the Sun all the way to the WNBA finals in 2022. Could the Valkyries take that philosophy a step further?

The Valkyries will have an early round playoff exit if…

The Valkyries struggle to score. During Golden State’s losses this season, they shot the ball from deep at a 30.4 percent clip, which is around 6 percentage points lower than in their wins. Their overall field goal percentage in losses (37.2) is over 16 percent lower than in wins (44.3).

Veteran Tiffany Hayes could be the key to countering what the general consensus says Golden State and their glaring weaknesses. When the stakes are highest and the Valkyries just need someone to go and get a bucket, who are they going to? Hayes will be ready to step up. She’s had a more modest role this season, playing 17 minutes a game rather than almost 27 the year prior. But this change in role was by design to ensure that Hayes was healthy enough for what head coach Natalie Nakase believes will be a long playoff run.

articles.title: Record WNBA viewership proves the league's drama is driving fans to screens, not away from them | Matt Calkins
articles.summary: WNBA ratings hit a record 1.37 million viewers this season as drama involving Caitlin Clark and league controversies fuel unprecedented attention.
articles.body: You're bored, and you want to convince your WNBA-loving friend that the league is a disaster. So you put together a list. You write down how the league's most popular player, Caitlin Clark, had her throat pushed in by Alyssa Thomas, but needed NBA Commissioner Adam Silver to step in and get Thomas suspended. You add how Caitlin is constantly left out of marketing campaigns, and was voted the 11th best guard in the WNBA by her peers. You throw in how the league's leaders still can't define what a woman is despite having a meeting on the subject. You jot down that teams regularly ban media (see: OutKick) they suspect will ask unflattering questions. You conclude with commissioner Cathy Engelbert once dismissing a fair question about her future by saying "I wonder whether you would ask that of a man," then note that she will retire after 2026. CAITLIN CLARK HELPS FEVER DELIVER WNBA'S LARGEST REGULAR-SEASON TV AUDIENCE IN 29 YEARS You give the list to your buddy. He just smiles. Check the TV ratings and attendance figures, he says. Shoot. He might just have you. Folks can complain about the WNBA being a circus all they want, but circuses tend to draw a lot of people into the tent. One could argue that the league has done a number on its reputation, but you can't argue with the number of eyeballs watching its teams. The WNBA averaged a record 1.37 million viewers across the ESPN networks during this regular season, which marked a 17% increase from last year. NBC and CBS also averaged at least one million viewers for their WNBA packages in 2026. And it's not just the broadcasts luring in fans. The league drew a record 3.79 million live attendees across 330 games, which is a 20.5% increase from last season. Yes, the two expansion teams inflated these numbers, but the average WNBA attendance of 11,474 was still a 5% increase from last regular season. How much of this is cash cow Caitlin Clark being healthy after missing most of last season? That certainly helps, but this goes beyond CC. Games not involving the Fever averaged 984,000 viewers this regular season — up 24% from last year. You can't tell me that isn't significant. You can't look at those numbers and say the WNBA is self-destructing. Perhaps one could argue that viewership and attendance would be even higher if smarter leadership kept the controversies at bay. But maybe, just maybe — the controversies are what's behind this boost. WILL THE WNBA’S UNSERIOUS, WEEKLY SITCOM DESTROY ONE OF THE GREATEST OPPORTUNITIES FOR WOMEN ATHLETES? As much as tradition and physical excellence drive sports viewership, drama is every bit as crucial. And whether it's the players' contempt for Clark, Sophie Cunningham's pointing meme, or the league's genuflection to trans activists —theater has the WNBA in the news every day. I once described it as half basketball, half WWE. My dad corrected me on that — it's half basketball, half Real Housewives of Hoop. When Clark barks at refs, or yells at White, or gets chewed out by Fever assistant coach Briann January — we don't turn away. Fans condemn players such as Thomas or Chennedy Carter or Mabrey for malicious fouls on Caitlin, but they don't skip the next game. Natasha Cloud losing her mind on Enes Kanter for wearing a shirt with the definition of a woman on it? Absurd. But it was a talker for a good week. Coach after coach giving pro trans answers when asked about the separation of biological men and women? Predictable, but incessantly newsworthy. The maligning of Fever supporters as racist middle Americans invading the league? Infuriating. But while fans roll their eyes one second, they glue them to the TV the next. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! I'll admit I'm as guilty as anyone. In addition to everything above, the WNBA's cowardice in banning media makes me want to stage a personal boycott. And yet, when the Fever start their playoff series against the Aces Sunday, I'll be as invested in that as any NFL game. There's a lot of talk about how the actions of players, coaches and leaders prevent the WNBA from being taken seriously. But part of me wonders if most of them even care about being taken seriously. They have their money. They have their eyeballs. They have their culture. Respect from the everyman may be immaterial to them. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Like any reality show, the Real Housewives of Hoop will leave you teeming with anger and frustration. But you can't help but tune into the next episode.

articles.title: A look inside NBA’s first MVP Bob Pettit’s Milwaukee Hawks career as the Hall of Famer passes away at 93
articles.summary: Bob Pettit, one of the most important players in early NBA history, has died at the age of 93.
articles.body: Bob Pettit, one of the most important players in early NBA history, has died at the age of 93. The basketball legend spent his entire 11-season professional career with the Milwaukee Hawks (now Atlanta Hawks) franchise. He became a dominant scorer and rebounder and helped shape the power forward position.Pettit also made history as the first NBA Most Valuable Player. He won the award twice and was selected to the All-Star team in every season he played. His career included an NBA championship, multiple scoring records and a place among the greatest players of his generation.Who was Bob Pettit?Bob Pettit was a former American professional basketball player who became one of the NBA’s biggest stars during the 1950s and 1960s.Born in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Pettit initially faced difficulties in basketball. He was cut from his high school varsity team as a freshman and sophomore. He later grew several inches and developed into a star.“I practiced at night with a lamp in the window in my back bedroom, shooting baskets hour after hour,” Pettit once toldNBA.com. “I just learned trial-and-error. Repeat it, repeat it, repeat it. Finally, I learned something.”That work helped him become a standout player at Louisiana State University. Pettit led LSU to conference championships and helped the school reach its first NCAA Final Four in 1953.The Milwaukee Hawks selected Pettit with the second overall pick in the 1954 NBA Draft. The franchise later moved to St. Louis, but Pettit remained with the organization throughout his career.He immediately made an impact. Pettit averaged 20.4 points and 13.8 rebounds per game during his rookie season and won Rookie of the Year.In 1956, the NBA introduced its Most Valuable Player award. Pettit became the first player to win it. He captured the MVP award again during the 1958-59 season.Pettit was also a remarkable rebounder. He finished his career averaging 26.4 points and 16.2 rebounds per game. He averaged a double-double in every one of his 11 NBA seasons.His biggest team achievement came during the 1958 NBA Finals. The St. Louis Hawks faced the Boston Celtics and won the championship in six games.Pettit finished his NBA career with 20,880 points and 12,849 rebounds. He was an All-Star in all 11 seasons and won the All-Star Game MVP award four times.Pettit retired from professional basketball in 1965. He was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 1971.After basketball, he returned to Baton Rouge and worked in banking and financial consulting.The Hawks later retired his No. 9 jersey, preserving his place in franchise history. articles.title: For the Indiana Fever, the playoff spotlight has never been brighter as they match up with reigning champion Aces: 'Everybody's watching'
articles.summary: The Fever have been blocking out the noise all season. Can they keep it up and make a deep playoff run?
articles.body:
The text messages began flooding Makayla Timpson 's phone in August. Names of people she hadn't spoken to in years. New numbers she didn't recognize.

People who knew her even tangentially wanted to congratulate the second-year forward on moving into the starting lineup, where she stayed for the final 13 games of the regular season.

It's hard to miss such news when the Fever are inescapable.

"Everybody's watching," Timpson told Yahoo Sports the day of an Aug. 18 victory in Toronto . "All of our games are everywhere. We're the team with the games broadcasted all over the place."

The Fever concluded their 44-game regular season — the only team to play every game on national television — with a whimper. Their 86-66 loss to No. 1 seed Minnesota , combined with results elsewhere on the final day of the regular season, pushed them down into the No. 6 seed for the third consecutive season despite realistic expectations they would nab a top-four seed.

There are thoughts about that. Fans fire off takes on social media platforms in short and long form. Surely, there is chatter over meals in Indiana and everywhere else, given the team is regularly watched by more than 1 million people per game, a metric previously unthinkable. This is a defining characteristic of their entire 2026 season that included unrelenting speculation surrounding superstar Caitlin Clark and head coach Stephanie White verbally ripping an "online community" of divisiveness attempting to "hijack our league," among other topics.

For the Fever, it's all white noise. They have focused on blocking out everything — or nearly everything — that does not reside within their walls. The franchise's awards season marketing campaign leaned into the idea, sending out boomboxes and cassette tapes for each of its candidates. The jackets listed records and elite stats. The tapes played loud, coupled with tape hiss, a broadcast call of their highlights.

Everything featured the running tagline "We don't do quiet."

The postseason will give them the true answer. Will it be an early exit, or a loud stomp that they can live up to championship intentions amid the rising fervor that comes with such a stage? Because this Fever team, despite underperforming in the standings, remains a dangerous championship contender facing the ultimate final test.

"At this point, everybody's record is 0-0," Clark said after the finale. "We're going into the playoffs."

Their supercharged backcourt of MVP candidates Clark and Kelsey Mitchell lived up to the bill. Mitchell (24.7 ppg) — coming off a concerning Rhabdomyolysis condition in Game 5 of the 2025 semifinals — and Clark (22.3 ppg) — returning to form after missing all but 13 games of last season with soft tissue injuries — are second and third in average scoring.

Not on their team — in the entire league.

They lead the Fever's record-shattering offense (96 ppg), made up of a formerly mind-boggling 20 games scoring at least 100 points. The previous record was 11. Their 4,222 total points are nearly 200 more than the second-place Las Vegas Aces (4,025).

In the dark of the flashy numbers, the Fever underperformed, even considering the competition among the eight playoff teams is tight. Only one series matchup, the No. 1 Lynx versus No. 8 Liberty, had been decided by Thursday night. It took the final 64 seconds of the season for the Golden State Valkyries to finish off a 16-point comeback over the Los Angeles Sparks , securing the No. 2 seed and ultimately sending Sparks second-year leader Lynne Roberts packing .

They'll now have an uphill climb through the playoffs, first facing an experienced Las Vegas team beginning on the reigning champions' home court (Sunday, 4 p.m. ET). The Aces are on a run of three WNBA titles in four years, edging the injury-riddled "Hospital Fever" roster in a deciding semifinals Game 5 in Las Vegas last season. None of Clark, Mitchell or center Aliyah Boston , who missed the second half of the Lynx game due to a lower leg injury flare-up, were on the court for overtime. Aces center A'ja Wilson (26.2 ppg, league lead) is in line for a fifth MVP this October , and along with Jackie Young motor the WNBA's second-best offense (91.5 ppg).

The travel doesn't make it any less challenging for Indiana, which had a chance at the No. 4 seed and rights to host the first game of the series. Game 2 is on Wednesday in Indianapolis, and an if-necessary Game 3 back in Las Vegas on Friday. Indiana won the season series, 2-1, with the loss coming on a buzzer-beating bucket in overtime.

On Indiana's side of the bracket is No. 2 Golden State, a matchup that would put to bed (at least for this season) the philosophical argument that defense wins championships. While the Fever lead the league offensively, the Valkyries were far and away the WNBA's best defense throughout the year. They hold teams to under 75.1 points per game on average. The Fever scored 75, 88 and 90 against them, winning only the highest-scoring affair.

White said following the season finale loss that the Fever don't shoot as they did very often, a message of upside, that they got it out of their system. Despite good early looks that would usually spell big leads, few went down for Indiana on Thursday. It was their lowest field-goal percentage (34.3%) and scoring total (66 points) of the season, though the bench rode out the final quarter. They've scored fewer than 80 only five times. Four are losses.

"It's 0-0, and we're still playing basketball," White, who led the Fever to the Finals in 2015 before returning in 2025, said. "And so we flush this one, we learn from it, we grow from it, and we start our prep [for Vegas]."

The offense will need to carry them, studded by glimpses of elite defense at the right moments. It's that side of the ball that has let them down, and could spell their demise. They allow opponents on average 90.4 points per game, fifth-worst in the league and four places away from the Liberty (86.4), the next-closest playoff team. (The Aces took a step back on that side of the ball this year, entering the postseason sixth overall, allowing 85.8 ppg).

Rarely do teams lacking in defense lift the trophy. Nor do seeds outside the top four. Only in 2021 did a team seeded fifth or sixth reach the Finals, when the No. 6 Sky defeated the No. 5 Mercury, 3-1, in the former best-of-five format. Now a best-of-seven, the Fever have nine wins ahead of them to win the franchise's first championship since 2012 and only the second overall.

A championship window, such as the one in which the Fever reside, is always ready to close. It takes a future-focused front office to hold it open. The 2027 books will need a creative mathematician to keep it all together.

Mitchell, the franchise's longest-tenured player on a supermax $1.4 million deal, is an unrestricted free agent. Boston's EPIC deal provision will kick in at $1.47M. Clark, set to still make a rookie-deal $597,596, will be in line to sign one, including a higher salary next year. Sixth Player candidate Sophie Cunningham , point guard back-up Tyasha Harris , who sustained an ankle injury and had to be carried off on Thursday, and Myisha Hines-Allen , who moved to the bench, are all UFAs. The salary cap will increase a currently undetermined amount in the first offseason under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA) based on revenue-sharing.

Then there are players like Timpson, the Fever's second-round pick in the 2025 draft. She averaged 2.6 points in 7.1 minutes per game as a rookie, showing glimpses of upside but not enough consistency on a roster riddled with injuries. After the team overperformed to within minutes of a Finals appearance, the coaching staff traveled to Unrivaled in the offseason to challenge her; she returned to town early to hone in on the task at hand. She's averaging 9 points, 6.3 rebounds, 0.8 blocks and shooting 60% as a starter.

The franchise campaigned for her as Most Improved, with a set of earplugs to give to neighbors who "need to block out the noise" if it was "too loud." An animated photo of one of Timpson's monstrous, momentum-shifting blocks framed the front of the card. She is, White said last month, "a prime example of somebody who is a star in her role."

As if to underline the point that nothing about the Fever is subdued, the head coach is awaiting a Timpson dunk. The 6-2 rim-running forward has come so close in layup lines and practices, it's silly she hasn't done it.

It is a microcosm of the Fever themselves. The expectations are attainable. It's their opportunity to show it, and quiet the din that will be at its peak.

articles.title: NY Knicks Magical Title Run Turned Game of Thrones’ Jon Snow into a ‘Serious’ NYK Fan?
articles.summary: It seems that the New York Knicks‘ championship journey this spring was so magical that Game of Thrones star Kit […]
articles.body:
It seems that the New York Knicks ' championship journey this spring was so magical that Game of Thrones star Kit Harington went from not caring much about basketball to becoming a "serious" Knickerbocker fan.

Unless you were a fan of the Atlanta Hawks , P hiladelphia 76ers , Cleveland Cavaliers , or San Antonio Spurs , the Knicks' journey to their first NBA title in 53 years captured the hearts and minds of basketball fans around the country. And with good reason.

After losing back-to-back games to the Hawks in the quarterfinals, New York went on one of the most entertaining playoff runs in sports history. When they weren't absolutely crushing teams, they were the architects of two of the greatest comebacks in playoff history in Game 1 of the East Finals and Game 4 of the Finals. The Knicks' playoff run became must-see TV this spring and united New York in a way the city rarely sees.

NY Knicks converted Kit Harington into 'diehard' fan

Well, you can add the Englishman and actor from Game of Thrones to that list of people who were engrossed in the Knicks earlier this year. During a conversation with the Happy, Sad, Confused podcast, Harington revealed he was staying in New York throught the 2026 playoffs and admittedly jumped on the Knicks bandwagon.

The 39-year-old also disclosed that he was somehow lucky enough to be inside Madison Square Garden for their epic Game 4 come-from-behind win in the Finals. " I was so lucky," he confessed . "I was like so cheeky as well. I had no right to those tickets. I had zero right."

Harington then admitted he had been to very few basketball games in-person until that legendary game and it was why he felt "guilt" for having the tickets when passing serious Knicks fans on the street that night.

"But now, I consider myself quite a serious Knicks fan," Harington proclaimed.

articles.title: Former Duke forward Kon Knueppel goes down with offseason injury
articles.summary: After suffering a hamstring injury, Kon Knueppel's status for Charlotte's season opener against the Brooklyn Nets is in jeopardy.
articles.body:
Both Duke supporters and Charlotte Hornets fans were hit with bad news Friday, as it was revealed that Kon Knueppel suffered a left hamstring injury while training for the 2026-27 NBA season. Knueppel will be sidelined for the entire preseason and is expected to be re-evaluated during the first week of the regular season.

A season ago, Knueppel was exceptionally durable, playing in 81 of 82 regular season contests. The former Blue Devil shot the ball incredibly well, averaging 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 0.7 steals while shooting 42.5% from beyond the arc.

Knueppel also led the league in 3-pointers made while breaking the rookie record for 3-pointers made in a season. Hopefully for Charlotte and Knueppel, he'll be able to return to the court as soon as possible. The Hornets begin their season October 21 against the Brooklyn Nets .

articles.title: Luka Doncic Doesn't Want to Be Lakers' GM After LeBron's Exit for 76ers, Says Rob Pelinka
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is weighing in but not taking over on Los Angeles Lakers roster and coaching decisions following LeBron James' free agency departure, according to general manager Rob Pelinka.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić is weighing in but not taking over on Los Angeles Lakers roster and coaching decisions following LeBron James' free agency departure, according to general manager Rob Pelinka.

"I feel like we're co-creators with him, because he's a very creative basketball mind," Pelinka said about Dončić in a Friday appearance on ESPN LA's Mason & Ireland Show (4:20 mark of the video below).

"Ultimately, I have the final responsibility to make calls on the roster, and Luka is very clear, like, 'I want you to do your job. I don't want to be the GM. I don't want to be the coach... but, we can co-create. Let's share ideas. Let's break down pros and cons and look at all aspects of a potential decision point before we make it.'"

Rumors of James' involvement in Lakers roster decisions popped up frequently during his eight-year tenure in Los Angeles.

ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported in 2022 Pelinka was reportedly "allowing for greater influence from [James] when it comes to personnel decisions than in the typical player-management relationship," including regarding the Lakers' 2021 trade for Russell Westbrook.

Both Pelinka and coach JJ Redick have recently expressed excitement about working with a new-look Lakers roster built around Dončić. Redick said in a Thursday press conference he felt this season was "probably the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together."

The Lakers are preparing to test out their new starting lineup featuring returners Dončić and Austin Reaves alongside offseason addition Walker Kessler when tipping off the regular season Oct. 21 against the visiting Golden State Warriors.

articles.title: El Valencia Basket somete al Casademont Zaragoza y luchará por el título (73-84)
articles.standfirst: Peterson (19+3+3), Araujo (17+2+3) y Buenavida (14+7+3) comandan el triunfo taronja
articles.summary: Peterson (19+3+3), Araujo (17+2+3) y Buenavida (14+7+3) comandan el triunfo taronja
articles.body: El Valencia Basket se convirtió este sábado en el primer finalista de la Supercopa LF Endesa tras derrotar por 73-84 al vigente campeón, el Casademont Zaragoza, en la semifinal disputada en el pabellón Jorge Garbajosa de Torrejón de Ardoz (Madrid). Su rival por el título saldrá de la segunda semifinal, que enfrenta a partir de las 20.00 horas en el mismo escenario al Innova-tsn Leganés y el Hozono Global Jairis de Alcantarilla (Murcia). La 'final anticipada' entre mañas y valencianas abrió el telón de la temporada 2026-27. Partido de reencuentros por parte de ambos conjuntos. El más mediático el de la internacional Helena Pueyo, que recibió una pitada por haber firmado por las taronja este mismo verano procedente de Zaragoza, donde fue una de las referentes las últimas dos temporadas. Además de Hempe, Fingall y Vitola que en su día jugaron en Valencia. Carlos Cantero apostó de inicio por su quinteto de confianza en un Zaragoza que defendía título tras ganar su primera Supercopa la temporada pasada. Sin embargo, la tenaz base Alexis Peterson se hizo con los mandos del partido en los compases iniciales anotando cuatro puntos para Valencia Basket. La imprecisión en tiros de campo (5 de 18) lastró a Casademont y las valencianas, muy intensas, se llevaron un primer asalto (14-22) que dejó el debut de dos prometedoras jóvenes con el primer equipo, la base Isa Hernández y la pívot Amelia Alonso, ambas con apenas 16 años. Araújo con un bonito aro pasado que terminó en 2+1 y un triple de forma consecutiva aumentó la distancia de +17 para las actuales campeonas de Liga y Copa a falta de 04:26 del segundo cuarto. Mariona Ortiz lideró una tímida reacción de las aragonesas para marcharse a vestuarios -9 puntos abajo. En la reanudación, Casademont mostró otra cara. Alentadas por su afición y su famoso lema "Zaragoza nunca se rinde", sus jugadoras acercaban el tanteo en el marcador gracias al tesón de Hempe y las incursiones de la checa Vorackova. Con las taronja en shock en los últimos minutos del tercer período, el conjunto maño aprovechó ser un bloque más consolidado y empató el choque 56-56 a falta de 01:14 y culminó la remontada al inicio del cuarto final con dos penetraciones de Laia Flores (61-58). En el momento decisivo, al rescate de Valencia salieron las Elenas (Buenavida y Pueyo), que con seis puntos seguidos daban aire a su equipo y un triple de la balear a falta de 2:54 para la conclusión fue una daga directa a las ilusiones zaragocistas (+11 de ventaja). De esta forma, Javi Torralba se estrenó con victoria en el banquillo valencianista (73-84) y su equipo luchará este domingo por levantar su cuarto título de Supercopa tras los conquistados en 2021, 2023 y 2024. 73 – Zaragoza (14+17+26+16): Ortiz (11), Sheppard (15), Vorackova (13), Vitola (-), Hempe (7) -quinteto inicial-, Fingall (2), Flores (9), Garzon (1), Oma (3), Hermosa (6), Cuevas (-) y Brito (-). 84 – Valencia (22+18+18+26): Peterson (20), Chery (3), Pueyo (10), Jenkins (-), Borkowska (4) -quinteto inicial-, Takacs-Kiss (8), Balogun (5), Buenavida (14), Araújo (17), Romero (1), Hernández (2) y Alonso (-). articles.title: Matt Thomas, refuerzo de emergencia con pedigrí NBA para el Unicaja
articles.standfirst: El escolta estadounidense llega al Unicaja por dos meses para cubrir la baja de Kalinoski, con opción de continuar hasta final de temporada
articles.summary: El escolta estadounidense llega al Unicaja por dos meses para cubrir la baja de Kalinoski, con opción de continuar hasta final de temporada
articles.body: El Unicaja tira de experiencia para cubrir una baja sensible. El conjunto malagueño ha cerrado la incorporación temporal de Matt Thomas, un escolta estadounidense de 32 años y 1,91 metros que llega para ocupar el hueco dejado por Tyler Kalinoski, lesionado. El acuerdo contempla inicialmente dos meses, aunque existe una opción para prolongar su estancia hasta final de temporada. Thomas no necesita demasiadas presentaciones en la Liga Endesa. Su primera aventura profesional fue en el Obradoiro, donde irrumpió con fuerza en la temporada 2017-18 (15,4 puntos por partido) y se ganó el salto al Valencia Basket. Allí conquistó la EuroCup y confirmó una de sus grandes señas de identidad: la puntería desde el perímetro, llegando a firmar un espectacular 47,7% en triples en aquella competición. Su buen rendimiento en España le abrió las puertas de la NBA. Raptors, Jazz y Bulls fueron sus destinos entre 2019 y 2022, con 126 partidos disputados y un notable 40,4% de acierto desde la línea de tres. Después regresó a Europa para jugar en Panathinaikos y ALBA Berlín, donde recuperó protagonismo, especialmente en su segunda temporada en Alemania, antes de volver a la ACB con el Coviran Granada. Precisamente en Granada volvió a exhibir su versión más reconocible: 14,6 puntos por partido y tres triples anotados de media, con un 46,1% de acierto. Después pasó por el Besiktas y ahora aterriza en Málaga para apagar un incendio puntual. El Unicaja incorpora así a un jugador que conoce la competición, tiene experiencia al máximo nivel y puede aportar desde el primer día una de las armas que más cotizan en Europa: puntos y amenaza exterior.

articles.title: Kyrie Irving Talks Mavericks Future in Video Amid NBA Trade Rumors, 'I'm In Love With This Place'
articles.summary: Kyrie Irving expressed love for his city but came short of saying he expects to retire a Dallas Maverick amid trade rumors surrounding him ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
Kyrie Irving expressed love for his city but came short of saying he expects to retire a Dallas Maverick amid trade rumors surrounding him ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season.

"I'm in love with this place just because of how welcoming it was, not just from the franchise aspect but also the fans, a lot of support around the city," Irving said Saturday (h/t DLLS Sports' Kevin Gray Jr).

When asked if he wants to finish his career in Dallas, Irving said, "I wish a lot of that was under my control, but I think it's a collaborative effort here."

Irving added he feels the Mavericks are ready to build "something new" after winning just 26 games last season as Irving rehabilitated from his ACL injury.

"I think I'm turning the page, and looking forward to building something new, having these guys rally around each other, I'll rally around them," Irving said. "They lean on me for leadership. I lean on them for energy, and vice versa."

Irving continued, "Every fair criticism that was brought to this franchise was fair. I'm never going to shy away from that, either. But I think my focus is just continuing to develop."

ESPN's Tim MacMahon recently reported how long Irving will be with the Mavericks is a question "being asked around the league" not because of discord between Irving and the Mavericks but the franchise may look to build a younger core around 19-year-old Cooper Flagg.

Irving, who turned 34 in March, is currently signed through this season with a player option for the 2027-28 campaign.

Whether he gets the chance to consider activating that option in Dallas could hinge on if new Mavericks general manager Mike Schmitz determines trading Irving by next February's deadline will give his franchise a better chance of building a playoff contender in Flagg's near future.

articles.title: Fever guard Ty Harris ruled out for 2026 WNBA playoffs after suffering broken left fibula in regular-season finale
articles.summary: Harris was carried off the court in Indiana's loss to the Lynx on Thursday.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Tyasha Harris will miss the 2026 postseason after breaking her left fibula, the team announced Saturday.

Harris suffered the injury during the Fever's regular-season finale on Thursday, going down in pain after a missed layup in the third quarter. The guard had to be carried off the court by staff, who took her back into the locker room.

Harris was ruled out shortly afterward, with the team initially citing an ankle injury.

Harris, 28, signed with Indiana ahead of the 2026 season. The guard averaged about 4 points, 2 assists and 1.1 rebounds per game coming off the bench.

The Fever also lost Aliyah Boston earlier in the game to a right lower leg injury, with head coach Stephanie White saying postgame that Boston experienced a flare-up of an injury she'd been dealing with throughout the season.

Indiana was held to a season low in points in the 86-66 loss to the Lynx. With the loss, the Fever fell to the sixth seed in the WNBA standings, setting up a high-pressure first-round matchup against the No. 3 Las Vegas Aces .

articles.title: El Innova-TSN Leganés barre al Hozono Global Jairis (69-50) y jugará la final
articles.standfirst: La pívot Aminata Sangare (29 puntos, 9 rebotes y 35 de valoración) comanda el triunfo de las.pepineras, que se verán con el Valencia Basket en la final (17.00 h)
articles.summary: La pívot Aminata Sangare (29 puntos, 9 rebotes y 35 de valoración) comanda el triunfo de las.pepineras, que se verán con el Valencia Basket en la final (17.00 h)
articles.body: El Innova-tsn Leganés hizo historia este sábado al imponerse al Hozono Global Jairis con una contundente y merecida victoria (69-50) en la semifinal de la Supercopa LF Endesa, por lo que luchará por su primer título en la competición ante el Valencia Basket en Torrejón de Ardoz (Madrid). La pívot Aminata Sangare firmó una soberbia actuación en el pabellón Jorge Garbajosa con 29 puntos, 9 rebotes y 35 de valoración. La segunda semifinal del sábado deparó un duelo entre el Leganés, que debutó en una Supercopa y el conjunto murciano, siempre competitivo y sorprendente en torneos cortos. Las locales salieron lanzadas al partido, primero imponiendo su ritmo de juego con un 7-0 inicial y con una desatada Aminata Sangare (11 puntos en los primeros minutos), que aumentó la ventaja hasta el 16-5. Bernat Canut se vio obligado a parar el partido para buscar soluciones, que llegaron en forma de penetraciones agresivas a canasta. La sevillana Alba Prieto, que volvía a jugar contra su exequipo y la escolta Sami Hill que comandaron la ofensiva de las de Alcantarilla, pero no evitaron que las azulonas cerrasen 21-12 el primer cuarto. El equipo de la Región de Murcia echó en falta a Lou López-Sénéchal, su principal referencia ofensiva, por estar recuperándose de una lesión en la rodilla. El 'Lega' controló el marcador y se gustó sobre el parqué, como demostró un efusivo gesto con las manos de María Espín a sus compañeras para celebrar una canasta sobre la bocina de Sangare. Al descanso, ocho puntos de ventaja para las de Javier Fort y con un Jairis incómodo, incapaz de encontrar ventajas ofensivas ante la intensa defensa de las madrileñas. Prueba de ello, el bajo porcentaje de acierto de dos (28%), además de que las pepineras aprovechaban la ventaja física en la pintura y en el rebote, a lo que se sumó que Laura Gil se cargó rápido con tres faltas personales. En la reanudación, los ataques locales buscaron hacer daño con balones en la zona, pero las de Alcantarilla demostraron garra y carácter y redujeron la desventaja a cuatro puntos (40-36). Sin embargo, el primer intento de reacción fue un espejismo y la solidez de las de la capital les daba alas. Una puerta atrás de bella factura de Elena Rodríguez y una bandeja de Regina Aguilar aumentaron la ventaja al final del tercero (49-37). La segunda tentativa llegó a mediados del último período cuando las de Canut redujeron de nuevo la ventaja a cuatro puntos tirando de veteranía. Pero el baloncesto es un deporte de estados de ánimo y un crecido Leganés, con una imperial Sangare (7 puntos consecutivos al ritmo de los cánticos de "mvp, mvp" de la grada) no dio opción al Jairis, vengándose así del enfrentamiento entre ambas en los cuartos de la pasada Copa de la Reina, cuando ocurrió todo lo contrario. Este partido será recordado como uno de los más importantes en la historia de las pepineras, que llenas de ilusión buscarán su primer título de Supercopa y se las verá ante Valencia Basket en la final, que se disputará este domingo a las 17:00 horas en el pabellón Jorge Garbajosa. 69 – Leganés (21+13+18+20): Lahuerta (3), Driessen (5), Sangare (29), Joiner (6), Igbokwe (13) -quinteto inicial-, Espín (3), Sahie (2), Gil (-), Aguilar (2), Rodríguez (4), Omoruyi (2) y Rosic (-), 50 – Jairis (12+14+13+13): Ayuso (14), Alarcón (2), Hill (6), Hobbs (5), Gil (7) -quinteto inicial-, Mané (2), Prieto (6), López (-), Costa (-), Alsina (3), Bessoir (-) y Massey (5). articles.summary: Childress (18+4 asistencias), Dos Anjos (12+8) y Soriano (15+5) lideran el ataque santiagués
articles.body: El Monbus Obradoiro, con un brillante Brandon Childress (18 puntos, 4 asistencias y 20 de valoración), volvió a la Liga ACB con una victoria por 85-90 ante un renovado MoraBanc Andorra. La puesta en escena del nuevo proyecto del MoraBanc Andorra fue inmejorable. El equipo dirigido por Žan Tabak, en los primeros 5 minutos, dio la 'bienvenida' a la Liga ACB al Monbus Obradoiro con un parcial de 14-2 con dos triples consecutivos de 'Chumi' Ortega y uno de Kassius Robertson. Los de Diego Epifanio, 'Epi', fueron a remolque con malas decisiones en ataque y una defensa endeble. Totalmente superados, llegaron a perder poe 24-11 y Lazar Mutic cerró el primer acto con un triple sobre la bocina para el 27-14. El Monbus Obradoiro despertó en el segundo cuarto y lo hizo primero con un parcial de 2-8 para el 29-22 con cuatro puntos seguidos del exjugador del MoraBanc Felipe Dos Anjos. Seis puntos seguidos del veterano pivot León Radošević pararon la reacción de los de 'Epi', pero volvieron con un parcial de 4-10 para acercarse a un punto (39-38). En ningún momento el Monbus Obradoiro completó la remontada y un 'alley-hoop' de Radošević (10 puntos y 17 de valoración) llevó el partido al descanso con un 46-43. En el tercer acto, el MoraBanc dominó al Monbus Obradoiro, pero sin conseguir diferencias altas en el electrónico. La máxima fue de +10 (68-58). Los de 'Epi' lucharon y cerraron un tercer cuarto igualado con un triple de Abogidi para dejar el 70-65 tras los terceros 10 minutos. Seis puntos consecutivos de Felipe Dos Anjos provocaron nervios a los locales con el 70-71 y una remontada completada. Dos triples seguidos, uno de Leo Meindl y otro de Barrueta, situaron el 74-77 a 4'45". A partir de entonces, el que fue a remolque fue el equipo de Žan Tabak. El dominio en la pintura fue de Joel Soriano, con 15 puntos, 5 rebotes y 18 de valoración. Un triple de Brandon Childress cerró el triunfo del equipo gallego en su vuelta a la ACB. 85 - MoraBanc Andorra (27+19+24+15): Akinjo (9), Robertson (15), 'Chumi' Ortega (6), 'Wes' Iwundu (12) y Pustovyi (12) -cinco inicial-; Kuric (5), Mutic (5), Rafa Luz (-), Radošević (10), Best (9) y Owen Aquino (2). 90 - Monbus Obradoiro (14+29+22+25): Childress (18), Barcello (6), Leo Meindl (12), Alejandro Galán (2) y Joel Soriano (15) -cinco inicial-; Abogidi (5), Sergi Quintela (2), Agada (7), Dos Anjos (12), Barrueta (11) y Brito (-). Árbitros: Emilio Pérez Pizarro, 'Juande' Oyón y Vicente Martínez. Sin eliminados. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la primera jornada de la Liga ACB disputado en el Pavelló Toni Martí de Andorra la Vella ante 3.848 espectadores.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton Shares New Pacers Hype Video Ahead of Return from Injury, 'Almost That Time'
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton shared a hype video of him and his teammates working out at Vanderbilt University in Nashville for the team's annual players-only minicamp as they prepare for the season.
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton shared a hype video of him and his teammates working out at Vanderbilt University in Nashville for the team's annual players-only minicamp as they prepare for the season.

The minicamp, which took place in mid-September, showcased Haliburton getting heavy work in with the Pacers.

Haliburton suffered a torn right Achilles tendon in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, and that cost him the entire 2025-26 campaign.

The two-time All-NBA selection previously confirmed in August that he's 100 percent cleared and ready to go for the season.

The Pacers begin training camp on Tuesday.

articles.title: Un gigante con los más pequeños
articles.standfirst: El exjugador del Real Madrid de baloncesto, Fernando Romay, se divierte en Plaza de España jugando con los más jóvenes
articles.summary: El exjugador del Real Madrid de baloncesto, Fernando Romay, se divierte en Plaza de España jugando con los más jóvenes
articles.body: “Yo le puse un tapón a Jordan”, es lo que suele recordar Fernando Romay. Hoy, por un instante, volvió a recordar esos tiempos junto con los más pequeños en la Noche del Deporte. Un gigante de 2,13 metros de altura ayudando a que los jóvenes anotaran sus lanzamientos. Un momento mágico que solo podía vivirse en Plaza de España. Los niños reclamaban a su héroe. El exjugador del Real Madrid y 174 veces internacional con la Selección Española estuvo 17 temporadas en el club blanco. Ahí ganó 21 títulos (7 Ligas, 5 Copas y 2 Copas de Europa, entre otros). En la absoluta brilló en los años 80. Si bien rodeado de super estrellas, en aquella época los centímetros en el baloncesto español brillaban por su ausencia. El pívot, también conocido como el 'gigante', ayudó al equipo en su camino a la medalla de plata en Los Ángeles 84. Aunque los jóvenes presentes en la aclamada y abarrotada plaza no conocen su historia, cualquiera identifica la figura de una leyenda como Fernando Romay. En la IV edición de La Noche del Deporte, Fernando brilló entre la gente en su vuelta a una pista de baloncesto. Las calles no han olvidado a su ídolo, el mismo que un día hizo disparar por los aires la atención por el deporte español. De uno en uno, entre niños y algún adulto, Romay controlaba que los lanzamientos entraran a canasta. En el Real Madrid, el jugador español promedió un 71,6 % de efectividad en tiros libres, hoy, fue el turno de los fans del baloncesto. Fernando, que también tuvo tiempo de atender a los micrófonos de MARCA, remarcó la importancia de la cantera española: "El baloncesto español debería dar más oportunidades a la cantera. No es normal que España haya ganado el mundial sub17 y los equipos fichen a jugadores de fuera. Faltan oportunidades". Aprovechó para alabar al seleccionador español: "Me gusta la España de Chus Mateo. Si hay alguien que pueda hacer funcionar a la selección, es él". Y quiso cerrar con una predicción de los ganadores de la ACB y la Euroliga: "Soy muy malo haciendo predicciones, pero diría el Real Madrid en la Euroliga. Y en la ACB, aunque me guste mucho el equipo del Valencia, mi corazón dice Real Madrid", declaró el 'gigante' español.

articles.title: Deuce McBride 'Disappointed' with Knicks Contract Talks, 'I'd Love to Get Something Done'
articles.summary: New York Knicks guard Miles "Deuce" McBride is entering the final season of a three-year, $13 million contract that pays him just under $4 million in 2026-27. He's scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent next offseason unless he and the Knicks can agree to terms on a new deal.
articles.body:
New York Knicks guard Miles "Deuce" McBride is entering the final season of a three-year, $13 million contract that pays him just under $4 million in 2026-27. He's scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent next offseason unless he and the Knicks can agree to terms on a new deal.

McBride has made it abundantly clear that he wants to stay in New York, based on a recent discussion he had with Kristian Winfield of the New York Daily News .

"I'm a little disappointed," McBride told Winfield regarding the fact that an extension hasn't transpired yet. "I want to be in New York. So yeah, it's a little hard at times. I've played through injury. I've been through a lot with this team. So you know, I'd love to get something done."

The 26-year-old McBride has played all five of his NBA seasons with the Knicks, who selected the former West Virginia star with the 36th overall choice in the 2021 NBA draft.

McBride dealt with a high ankle sprain and core muscle injury last year and played just 41 games, but the ailments didn't stop him from averaging a career-high 12.0 points per game while shooting 41.3 percent from three. He saw 26.3 minutes per contest, ranking sixth on the Knicks in playing time.

The guard feels confident in what he's shown so far, particularly his ability to improve each season.

"I feel like in times where guys have been out, I've been able to show a lot," McBride said. "So it's always — to me — it's about opportunity. I feel like I've continued to grow and improve every single year."

Lee Escobedo of the Knick of Time Show provided a theory about why McBride hasn't been extended:

"New York passed on a new deal, and a rule in the collective bargaining agreement explains why. A veteran extension carries a six-month trade restriction when it runs past four total seasons, raises first-year salary more than 20 percent, or includes later raises above 5%. Any deal worth signing for a player at $3.9 million trips all three. Six months from an August signature lands past the February trade deadline, which means extending Deuce McBride and trading him stopped being compatible sometime in early August."

We'll see what happens regarding McBride's Knicks future soon enough. In the meantime, he's set to play another key role off the bench for the defending NBA champions, who begin their season on Tuesday, Oct. 20 at home against the Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.title: Un gigante brilla en la bacanal ofensiva del Palau
articles.standfirst: El pívot (21+6 y 30 de valoración) lidera el triunfo del Barça ante un buen Leyma Coruña
articles.summary: El pívot (21+6 y 30 de valoración) lidera el triunfo del Barça ante un buen Leyma Coruña
articles.body: El Barça se estrenó este sábado en la Liga Endesa con un triunfo sin piedad por 119-101 ante el recién ascendido Leyma Coruña en un duelo que no se rompió hasta el último cuarto. El pívot Olek Balcerowski, con 21 puntos, fue el máximo anotador del partido. En los visitantes, el jugador con más puntos fue el base Alonzo Verge, con 16. Los azulgranas arrancaron mejor el partido de la mano de su jugador más en forma, Joel Parra, que anotó con facilidad con su juego de pies en el poste bajo (12-7, min. 5). Sin embargo, los visitantes no se escondieron ni mucho menos y lograron darle la vuelta al marcador con la entrada a pista de Dídac Cuevas, con un descaro que provocó el tiempo muerto de Sekulic (14-15, min. 8). El tramo final de primer periodo se convirtió en un intercambio de canastas que dejó al Barça por delante con un ajustado 22-18. El guion no cambió en el segundo cuarto, aunque el Barça abrió una pequeña brecha en el luminoso con la entrada a pista de Agustín Ubal, que puso el 29-23 y provocó el parón de Marco (29-23, min. 13). Cuando parecía que los locales podían escaparse en el marcador, el Leyma Coruña puso la sexta marcha en el acelerador y volvió a ponerse por delante tras unos buenos minutos de Caio Pacheco desde la zona exterior (36-38, min. 17). Los visitantes mantuvieron el acierto ofensivo en el tramo final de primera mitad, pero un recital de Juan Núñez en la dirección de juego y el poderío interior de Olek Balcerowski dejaron a los azulgranas con un 52-47 en el tiempo de descanso. En la reanudación, el Barça puso un +9 en un abrir y cerrar de ojos gracias al juego en transición veloz de Justin Robinson, que fue un mal de cabeza para la defensa visitante (59-50, min. 22). Como pasó antes, los de Sekulic intentaron sentenciar el choque, pero el Leyma Coruña no se rindió y tres triples prácticamente consecutivos de Guillem Jou les metieron de lleno en el encuentro (75-69, min. 28). El equipo visitante llegó a ponerse a tan sólo tres puntos, pero de nuevo una canasta sobre la bocina de Balcerowski puso el 85-79 al final del tercer cuarto, un resultado bastante ajustado de cara a los últimos diez minutos de partido. Ya en el último periodo, Robinson lideró a su equipo y con un parcial de 6-0 en un minuto, el Barça superó los diez puntos de ventaja y puso tierra de por medio en el Palau Blaugrana (90-79, min. 31). A diferencia de los cuartos anteriores, el Barça no dejó que hubiera reacción alguna en el conjunto gallego y el partido se rompió muy rápidamente mediante los triples de Umoja Gibson (105-88, min. 36). Al final, el Barça venció por 119-101 al Leyma Coruña para estrenarse en la Liga Endesa 2026-27 con victoria. 119. articles.title: Buddy Hield Traded to Bulls from Hornets for Former Lottery Pick, New NBA Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Buddy Hield is on the move again days after being traded from the Atlanta Hawks to the Charlotte Hornets.
articles.body:
Buddy Hield is on the move again days after being traded from the Atlanta Hawks to the Charlotte Hornets.

The Hornets are trading Hield and cash to the Chicago Bulls in exchange for Rob Dillingham, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Saturday.

Charania reported Thursday the Hawks had traded Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash to the Hornets in exchange for Dorian Finney-Smith.

Hield split last season between the Golden State Warriors and Hawks. He is signed through next season under a $9.7 million cap hit with a $10 million player option for 2027-28, per Spotrac .

According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, Hield was able to be moved twice in a week because the original trade from the Hawks to Hornets did not involve aggregating his salary with another player's.

The Bulls are projected to go over the salary cap following the trade but remain more than $34 million below the luxury tax, per Spotrac's Keith Smith. Smith also projects the Hornets will drop to $25.6 million beneath the luxury tax.

Dillingham is set to play this season under a $6.9 million cap hit after the Bulls activated his team option.

He holds an $8.8 million club option on which the Hornets will need to make a decision by Oct. 31, per Spotrac .

The Hornets could either create a $2.8 million trade exception or use the $8.2 million trade exception gained from trading Collin Sexton to the Bulls in February in order to accommodate Dillingham's contract, per Marks.

Should the Hornets use the Sexton trade exception for the deal, they could also create a $9.7 million trade exception for Hield, per Smith .

Charlotte still has to move some players from the roster in order to hit the 15-man limit by Oct. 19, Marks noted.

Dillingham was initially a costly addition for the Minnesota Timberwolves ahead of the 2024-25 season.

The Wolves sent a package including an unprotected 2031 first-rounder for the chance to acquire the rights to Dillingham, who had been selected by the San Antonio Spurs with the No. 8 pick in the 2024 draft.

Dillingham ultimately saw limited playing time while coming off the bench for a season-and-a-half with the Wolves before he was traded to the Bulls as part of the trade-deadline deal that sent Ayo Dosunmu to Minnesota last February.

The Hornets could now hope Dillingham, who struggled to produce in his brief tenure with Chicago, will benefit from another change of scenery.

The Bulls will meanwhile bring in Hield as a veteran presence who can add shooting abilities and experience to what may be one of the NBA's youngest rosters next season.

articles.title: Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla joins Tim Tebow in distancing himself from Life Surge after 'scam' allegations
articles.summary: Mazzulla and Tebow are far from the only sports figures tied to Life Surge.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla was one of the many sports figures connected to Christian organization Life Surge when allegations emerged of predatory financial practices.

Mazzulla previously spoke at a Life Surge event in Portland, Maine last September and was scheduled to do another in Hartford, Connecticut on Oct. 17. He has reportedly informed the organization he will no longer attend the Hartford event and requested his image be removed from its website.

"Once these [allegations] came out, I just completely backed out of it. I'm not showing up there and obviously don't support any of the allegations or things that they're accused of, and [I'm] moving forward."

The allegations against Life Surge came via a co-investigation by the podcast "Pablo Torre Finds Out" and Kiera Butler of Mother Jones . Mazzulla was one of dozens of celebrities paid to draw attendees to a relatively cheap introductory event, at which point the people would be pushed into a cascading series of financial education classes, such as how to make money from the stock market or real estate.

These classes were not cheap. After an initial $97 class, packages would reportedly range from about $10,000 to $40,000, all presented as ways for attendees to enrich themselves and to help advance their Christian mission. Attendees who were not able to put money up front were allegedly encouraged to take out lines of credit with a third-party lender or draw from retirement accounts.

While those lines of credit reportedly started with low interest rates, if not zero, the variable interest rate would soon escalate to an unmanageable degree, allegedly leaving those involved in dire financial straits.

Mazzulla told the Globe he hopes those attendees will have the resources and guidance needed to regroup, but also won't let the matter impact his mission to do good via his religion:

"It's an unfortunate situation, but my purpose is to use my platform for a positive impact on faith," Mazzulla said. "The risk you take is situations like this happen. The most important thing is to No. 1, focus on the people who were wronged and No. 2, do the best job you can authentically and morally and ethically to share your faith without negatively impacting people."

The PTFO episode, titled "We Investigated the Christian 'Scam' Fronted by Tim Tebow," mostly focuses on Tebow, who was reportedly paid between $50,000 and $100,000 per appearance and was on pace to appear at 23 different events across 2026. It's unclear how much Mazzulla was compensated for his appearance.

Tebow said Friday he is pausing his relationship with Life Surge as his team looks into the allegations, which he called "extremely, extremely serious."

In addition to Tebow and Mazzulla, a litany of former athletes and coaches have been connected to Life Surge through the investigations or the organization's own website: Joe Montana, Magic Johnson, Derek Carr, Marcus Mariota, Saquon Barkley, Cooper DeJean, Brandon Graham, Michael Strahan, Nick Foles, Nick Sirianni, David Ortiz, Russell Wilson, Dominique Dawes, Jerome Bettis, Darryl Strawberry, Emmitt Smith, Cris Carter, Mark Few, Jeremiah Smith, Calvin Johnson, Brian Dawkins, Bob Stoops, Brian Urlacher, Antonio Gates and David Robinson.

Former ESPN host Sage Steele is also alleged to have participated in 10 events in 2026 alone.

Mazzulla has been the Celtics' head coach since the 2022-23 season, reaching the playoffs in all four seasons so far and winning the NBA championship in 2023-24.

articles.title: Enes Freedom rips Cheryl Reeve for saying women's sports advocates 'don’t want transgender people to exist'
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom called on Cheryl Reeve to step down after the Lynx coach said the transgender athletes debate targets trans people's existence.
articles.body: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom pushed back against Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve after she claimed the debate over transgender athletes is part of a broader effort by critics who "don’t want transgender people to exist." Freedom responded to Reeve in a social media post Saturday, rejecting her characterization of those advocating to keep biological males out of women’s sports. "Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve should step down immediately. You can’t lead women’s basketball while refusing to stand up for women’s sports. Can someone, for the love of God, please explain to her that: Protecting women’s sports is not an attack on anyone’s existence, nor does it erase a community. Coach, if you truly mean what you just said, then put your hypocrisy aside and prove it by drafting me in the 2027 WNBA Draft," Freedom wrote. LYNX COACH CHERYL REEVE VOICES SUPPORT FOR THE TRANS COMMUNITY AGAIN AFTER REGULAR SEASON FINALE VS FEVER Reeve made the remarks after the Lynx closed the regular season with an 86-66 victory over the Indiana Fever at Target Center Thursday. The game was accompanied by competing demonstrations outside the arena over transgender participation in women’s sports. "I think that’s probably one of the more meaningful things that would mark the season for me," Reeve said. "It’s that the transgender community is one that deserves our support, and what is happening in the name of some issues of transgender in sports — it’s really an attack on all transgender community. They don’t want transgender people to exist." Reeve said the reaction she received after wearing a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt during a nationally televised Aug. 2 game against Indiana made the gesture one of the most meaningful moments of her season. "The amount of communication of people who were affected by something as simple as wearing a T-shirt in support of them and helping them be seen — with the platform that we have in professional sports, it was a small gesture by me," Reeve said. "It’s something I believe in, obviously, wholeheartedly." "If I could have helped just one to feel differently about themselves, because for the transgender community this really is about life and death for them," she continued. "The number of parents of transgender kids that I heard from and how it helped them and their families, it helped their child think differently about themselves and that there is someone in our position, like we have as a leader. To know that there are people out there that believe in them, that they belong." The comments marked at least the fourth time Reeve addressed the transgender issue during a WNBA media availability this season. WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT SENDS TRANS INCLUSION MEMO AFTER ENES FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE ANNOUNCEMENTS Reeve initially spoke about it following Supreme Court rulings that upheld state laws protecting women’s and girls’ sports. She later defended transgender participation before the Lynx’s first home game against the Fever, saying that "every kid has a right to sports" while acknowledging that eligibility becomes more complicated after puberty. The four-time WNBA champion coach also spoke privately with Fever guard Sophie Cunningham before their Aug. 2 matchup. Cunningham previously said she wanted to protect girls who should not have to compete against or share locker rooms with biological males, while emphasizing that she did not harbor hatred toward transgender people. "I think that I am here to extend love," Cunningham said. "But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men." Freedom inserted himself into the WNBA’s transgender debate in August by announcing that he intended to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft under the name "Enisa Freedom." He said the move was designed to test the league’s eligibility standards, which state that only women may play in the WNBA but do not publicly define eligibility through biological sex. ENES KANTER FREEDOM OPENS UP ON CONFRONTATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD THAT LED TO EJECTION, WNBA PURSUIT The former NBA center has repeatedly maintained that he is raising the issue seriously and is not attempting to demean transgender people. "I’m not here to mock, make fun of, or disrespect any group or anyone’s personal decisions," Freedom wrote in an earlier statement. "What I’m trying to do is bigger than clicks or attention." Freedom also publicly separated his campaign from the conduct of other former male basketball players who joined the WNBA draft effort, saying his goal had "never been publicity, political theater, cheap attention, or stunts." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Former NBA player Royce White also responded to Reeve’s latest remarks, but took a distinctly different approach from Freedom. While Freedom offered a direct rebuttal to Reeve’s characterization of women’s-sports advocates, White issued an overtly satirical statement promoting his female alter ego, "Roysha." "I appreciate Coach Reeve’s sentiment toward Transgenders," White wrote. "In these increasingly polarized times, it appears a potential source of cultural common ground has emerged ... Kweeen Roysha! Pay is the perfect blend of MAGA and mainstream. I think there’s a real opportunity to create a bridge, because a lot of conservatives nationwide would like to see Roysha play in the WNBA. The Minnesota Lynx would be a perfect home as the new transgender capital of America." The WNBA previously said there were no immediate transgender eligibility matters affecting the league and condemned what it called "bad-faith efforts" to demean or marginalize others. The league has never had a transgender woman play on a roster. Its collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA" but does not publicly provide a more detailed definition based on biological sex.
